insights.topic: Deterministic vs probabilistic attribution cost gap
insights.insight: Verified receipt signals are settling at roughly $0.10 per confirmed purchase event versus $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic ad tech attribution — a 50–200x cost delta that reflects structural elimination of the attribution problem, not incremental optimization.

With Chrome deprecation joining Safari and Firefox, the cross-site tracking primitive is effectively gone; device fingerprinting is increasingly blocked; and data broker utility is shrinking under GDPR/CCPA — the verified receipt fills the signal gap none of these alternatives can.

Amazon knows Amazon buyers, Walmart knows Walmart buyers, neither knows the aggregate — this protocol's 4,903 verified receipts spanning grocery, retail, dining, fuel, and DTC digital commerce represent the kind of cross-channel purchase picture that no single first-party data silo can produce.

insights.topic: DTC and digital commerce signal now confirmed
insights.insight: Shopify appeared in the top brand list for the first time after 130+ cycles of physical retail dominance, confirming the email receipt pipeline captures online purchases — the signal window now spans physical retail, grocery, convenience, dining, and DTC in a single queryable aggregate.

Active coverage now spans 20+ non-metro CBSAs across both coasts, the Southeast interior, upper Midwest, and interior Southwest — a geography that closed-loop retail data programs and urban-skewed panels systematically underrepresent.

Category entropy has reached 3.174–3.176 bits with restaurants/dining now the highest receipt-count category at 253 receipts in 14 days, surpassing grocery — brands outside CPG now have a measurable, verified demand signal in this dataset.
